items.title: Funding frenzy, chip wars, and robot dreams: Inside China‘s AI boom
items.author: Krystal Hu
items.creator: Krystal Hu
items.summary: OpenAI is continuing to attack Anthropic's home turf by trying to capture the most valuable use case in AI: coding.
items.body:
OpenAI is continuing to attack Anthropic's home turf by trying to capture the most valuable use case in AI: coding.
Airbnb (ABNB.O) is expanding its engineering and product teams’ access to GPT-6 Astra, OpenAI’s flagship model, CTO Ahmad Al-Dahle told me, as early testing shows how powerful the model can be.
Al-Dahle said the company will be adding it to the other models on offer for its engineers, encouraging them to use whichever model works best for the job. As he put it: "There isn't a sort of attachment to one model versus another. There's only what works better."
Airbnb’s move is an example of how a new powerful model could help OpenAI level the playing field against Anthropic's Claude Code, which has captured much of the coding market so far.
Airbnb also uses and post-trains open-source models for specific use cases, and says they can outperform frontier models in those cases.
Many of the best open-source models, notably, come from China.
Ahead of President Trump's [USN:L6N45E02J TEXT:"meeting with President Xi"] on Thursday, I called up the two reporters who probably know China's AI scene better than anyone — our Beijing colleagues, Eddie and Laurie. How did China get so good at open source, so fast? And do people there feel the same AI anxiety Americans do?
Scroll down for my Q&A with Eddie and Laurie — it'll get you up to speed on China's AI development in just a few minutes.
Secure your front row seat for exclusive Reuters AI conversations–sign up here to watch my colleagues’ live interview with US FTC Chairman Andrew Ferguson , and Joe Lonsdale , Founder of 8VC and Co-Founder of Palantir Technologies at Reuters Momentum AI this Friday.
OUR LATEST REPORTING IN TECH AND AI [USN:L6N45A0PY TEXT:"Ten days that changed the course of AI"]
[USN:L1N4570TA TEXT:"In Silicon Valley, AI data center boom meets local resistance"]
[USN:L6N45E0VY TEXT:"AI is changing how Americans choose snacks"]
[USN:L6N45E0SA TEXT:"Meta testing a 'human concierge' for its new personal AI agent, Muse"]
[USN:L6N45E0DO TEXT:"Ex-Google safety chief warns AI could harm children more than social media did"]
[USN:L6N45D0NY TEXT:"Three out of four Americans say AI firms not doing enough to prevent disaster"]
FUNDING FRENZY, CHIP WARS AND ROBOT DREAMS IN CHINA Eduardo Baptista and Laurie Chen are Reuters correspondents based in Beijing, where they cover China's technology and political landscape up close. They both speak fluent Mandarin and have a track record of breaking scoops by tracking China's AI boom from the inside. Our conversation has been edited for length and clarity.
Q: Why is there so much AI fundraising activity in China?
Eddie: It all comes down to compute. Over the past year, Chinese labs realized the same thing US labs did: if you want to compete at the frontier, you can’t avoid spending billions on advanced chips and data centers.
Take DeepSeek. It used to pride itself on not raising external capital, relying instead on Liang Wenfeng’s quant hedge fund High-Flyer. That’s no longer realistic. The next generation of models is so compute‑hungry that even DeepSeek has gone on a fundraising push and is now [USN:L4N4560GR TEXT:"preparing for a potential IPO"].
You see the same pattern with MiniMax, Z.ai, Moonshot, and others looking at Hong Kong listings or secondary share sales. All of this is essentially for raising money to buy compute.
Q: How much of this is funded by Beijing versus private capital?
Laurie: It’s a genuine mix of three: private capital and VCs; big tech and large private companies, as well as state-backed and state-owned funds.
Chinese researchers know they operate with far less compute than labs like OpenAI or Anthropic. That forces them to be more disciplined: fewer wild experiments, more targeted bets.
On the state side, you have vehicles like China’s national semiconductor investment fund taking stakes in companies such as DeepSeek. The government is strategic, not omnipresent — it wants influence in key players, but a lot of the frenzy is still driven by market investors chasing the next AI champion.
Q: There is lots of debate on AI safety in the US. Is China having the same debate?
Eddie: The tone is very different. In the US, you hear a lot of existential-risk talk. In China, the focus is more pragmatic. AI is seen as a way to squeeze growth and efficiency out of a tough economy — weak consumer sentiment, tight job markets, pressure on productivity.
Regulators like the Cyberspace Administration of China absolutely discuss AI agent risks, but it’s a dry, policy‑driven debate, not a public moral panic. The dominant question is still ‘how do we deploy this to help the economy?’ rather than ‘should we slow this down?’
Q: How big is China's AI data center build-out?
Eddie: Much smaller than many people think. When we looked through thousands of Chinese government documents on AI data centers, we found that OpenAI’s Stargate alone — a proposed half‑trillion‑dollar mega‑infrastructure plan — would cost about five times more than everything China has spent on AI data centers in the past five years. In China, typical AI data center projects cost hundreds of millions of dollars each and are spread across hundreds of smaller sites.
Q: With Nvidia constrained by US export controls, what chips is China using?
Eddie: Until 2023-24, Nvidia (NVDA.O) dominated a China AI chip market Nvidia’s CEO Jensen Huang has called a $50 billion opportunity. Export controls have effectively forced Nvidia to retreat from the highest end of that market.
That’s opened space for Huawei, which has become the de facto primary supplier for advanced AI workloads in China. Huawei knows it’s unlikely to match Nvidia’s single‑chip performance anytime soon, so its strategy is to build the best chip it can under sanctions, and use advanced packaging and network design to link thousands of chips into large systems, or “super nodes.” The goal is to try to compete at the system level, not the chip level.
The big questions are if Huawei's system architecture meaningfully narrows the gap with Nvidia, and if Huawei can scale fabrication and improve yields enough to meet domestic demand.
Until both answers are clearly yes, China’s AI compute capacity will remain constrained.
Q: Why is China so strong on open-source models?
Laurie: Initially, this wasn’t a political directive. Chinese labs recognized they were behind US frontier labs, so opening weights was a pragmatic way to accelerate collective learning and let researchers build on each other’s work.
Later, Beijing embraced open-weight models as a diplomatic tool, pitching them as a global public good for countries that lack their own frontier AI.
The problem is monetization. Many open-weight labs struggle to turn popularity into revenue.
Q: What about robotics and humanoids? Is China really ahead of the US?
Eddie: On hardware, China is very strong. Companies like Unitree, UBTECH, and others have made impressive gains in mobility and balance, dynamic control, and visually [USN:L6N44E0UQ TEXT:"striking performance demos"] — running, jumping, kung fu routines.
But what really matters is embodied AI software: models that let robots truly understand and operate in the physical world. That’s where the bottleneck is. Timelines are highly uncertain. As Unitree’s founder Wang Xingxing put it, a “ChatGPT moment” for embodied AI could be 2 to 3 years away if things go fast, or 5 to 10 years away if progress is slower.
If that software breakthrough doesn’t come, we could see failed business models, bankruptcies, and a sharp reset in robotics valuations.
Laurie: On cutting-edge embodied AI models, US startups are still slightly ahead. A recent example is a US company that showed a humanoid learning a new task from a single short video, with no lengthy retraining. When I asked a Chinese founder about it, he acknowledged that no Chinese team has matched that yet.
The race now is to build robots that can do general-purpose tasks, autonomously, with minimal data and training, and still hit high reliability. That’s where the real gap lies.
CHART OF THE WEEK Here's a number that could put Silicon Valley on notice: 73% of Americans don't think AI companies have done enough to prevent their technology from causing serious harm.
That's according to a [USN:L6N45D0NY TEXT:"new Reuters/Ipsos poll"] of 1,277 adults conducted September 17-20. Only 24% think the safeguards are adequate. For an industry that spends a lot of energy talking about "responsible AI," that's a pretty resounding vote of no confidence.
The skepticism doesn't stop there. More than half of respondents, 55%, said they'd welcome a slowdown in AI development, a striking number given how much the industry's narrative leans on speed as a competitive necessity. And this isn't a one-off blip: the same survey found 39% now see AI's impact on society as negative, the highest share since Reuters/Ipsos started asking in March, while just 11% call it a net positive. While the technology keeps improving, trust in it doesn't. Turns out those are two different problems.

items.title: Anthropic says Claude AI helped discover novel enzyme system
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Anthropic on Wednesday said its Claude model helped discover a novel enzyme system with properties reminiscent of mechanisms in gene-editing technology CRISPR, marking the first result from the AI startup's biology research efforts.
items.body:
Anthropic on Wednesday said its Claude model helped discover a novel enzyme system with properties reminiscent of mechanisms in gene-editing technology CRISPR, marking the first result from the AI startup's biology research efforts.
The finding comes days after Reuters reported Anthropic had quietly [USN:L1N45A0H1 TEXT:"established a wet lab"] in the San Francisco Bay Area, as the company expands its ambitions in life sciences and drug-related research beyond purely computer-based work.
Anthropic said Claude analyzed large DNA databases and found an unusual system built around a reverse transcriptase (RT), an enzyme that copies RNA into DNA.
Anthropic has named the system array-associated reverse transcriptases, or ART.
ART contains repeating DNA sequences that resemble patterns seen in CRISPR, Anthropic said.
The company noted that while the underlying RT had been identified in previous studies, Claude appeared to be the first to recognize key features of the broader system, including an array of non-coding DNA sequences and an additional protein of unknown function.

items.title: Hellman & Friedman explores sale of Applied Systems at up to $10 billion, sources say
items.author: Milana Vinn
items.creator: Milana Vinn
items.summary: Private equity firm Hellman & Friedman is exploring a sale of insurance software provider Applied Systems that could value the company at up to $10 billion, according to people familiar with the matter.
items.body:
Private equity firm Hellman & Friedman is exploring a sale of insurance software provider Applied Systems that could value the company at up to $10 billion, according to people familiar with the matter.
The private equity firm is working with investment bankers at JPMorgan (JPM.N) and Goldman Sachs (GS.N) on the process, which has attracted interest from prospective buyers, said the sources, who requested anonymity because the matter is confidential.
Applied Systems, Hellman & Friedman, JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs declined to comment.
Headquartered in Chicago, Applied Systems provides software that helps insurance agencies and brokerages manage customer relationships, policy administration, and other workflows. Its customers include insurance brokerages such as HUB International, Insurance Office of America, and the Baldwin Group, according to its website.
Applied Systems generates more than $550 million in annual earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, one of the sources said.
Hellman & Friedman bought Applied Systems from Bain Capital in a deal valued at approximately $1.8 billion in early 2014.
A sale would rank among the largest software buyout processes this year and test investor appetite for mature software assets, following ServiceNow's $7.7 billion acquisition of cybersecurity provider Armis and buyout firm Hg's $6.4 billion take-private of financial software provider OneStream.
Sell-side activity in the software sector has picked up in recent weeks after being relatively muted over the past months, with more companies launching sale processes.
This month, Reuters reported that Thoma Bravo was [USN:L6N44U168 TEXT:"exploring a sale"] of Foundation Software, Vista Equity Partners was [USN:L6N4560J1 TEXT:"considering a sale"] of banking software provider Finastra, and healthcare software company Waystar was [USN:L8N44T1P9 TEXT:"weighing strategic options"], including a sale, as sponsors seek to capitalize on improving valuations.

items.title: Vídeo de multidão não mostra Flávio em Recife, mas show em Campina Grande (PB)
items.author: Reuters Fact Check
items.creator: Reuters Fact Check
items.summary: Um vídeo de uma multidão na orla de uma cidade não mostra a passagem do candidato a presidente Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) por Recife, mas um show em Campina Grande (PB).
items.body:
Um vídeo de uma multidão na orla de uma cidade não mostra a passagem do candidato a presidente Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) por Recife, mas um show em Campina Grande (PB).
Estes são os principais detalhes:
“Aqui é Bolsonaro Recife”, diz uma postagem com o vídeo no Facebook .
Flávio teve agenda de campanha em Recife na última quarta-feira, mas as imagens não mostram seu comício na cidade.
O vídeo foi originalmente compartilhado no Instagram em 7 de junho deste ano pelo fotógrafo Rondinelle De Paula, a quem são creditadas as imagens.
“São mais de 10 anos cobrindo essa festa -- e sempre -- eu digo sempre irei me emocionar com a Namoradrilha do Spazzio. Salve @bellmarques, Salve Campina, Cidade do Maior São João do Mundo!”, escreveu na legenda.
A Namoradrilha é um bloco tradicional comandado pelo cantor Bell Marques que ocorre anualmente em Campina Grande no período junino.
Neste ano, o evento foi realizado em 7 de junho. Outros registros do bloco mostram um cenário semelhante ao do vídeo checado.
A Reuters confirmou pelo Google Street View que o vídeo foi feito em Campina Grande – nas imagens, aparece, por exemplo, o Museu de Arte Popular da Paraíba (MAPP).
Veredicto: Legenda errada. As imagens são de um show de Bell Marques em Campina Grande, e não da campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro em Recife.
Este artigo foi produzido pela equipe da Reuters Fact Check. Envie sugestões de checagem via WhatsApp pelo número (11) 91599-9278 . Leia mais sobre nosso trabalho de checagens de afirmações nas redes sociais aqui .

items.title: Europeans warn of rising Russian sabotage but see no imminent NATO attack
items.author: CNA
items.summary: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said Russia is increasing cyberattacks, sabotage and drone incursions "to scare Europe into winding down its support for Ukraine."

Europeans warn of rising Russian sabotage but see no imminent NATO attack

EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said Russia is increasing cyberattacks, sabotage and drone incursions "to scare Europe into winding down its support for Ukraine."

EU European Commission Vice-President Kaja Kallas on the sidelines of the ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Meeting at the Philippine International Convention Centre on Jul 24, 2026 in Pasay, Metro Manila, Philippines. (Photo: REUTERS/Ezra Acayan)

UNITED NATIONS: Russia is intensifying sabotage, cyberattacks and other hybrid attacks across Europe to undermine support for Ukraine, European ministers said, while dismissing concerns that Moscow is capable of launching a direct assault on NATO.
Speaking on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly this week, officials from countries on NATO's eastern flank said Moscow was increasingly using drone incursions, cyberattacks, sabotage and other covert operations to sow fear, test Western resolve and weaken backing for Kyiv.
"Europe faces a fast proliferation of sabotage attacks and airspace violations," EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas told reporters. "Moscow is trying to scare Europe into winding down its support for Ukraine."
European governments increasingly see Russia's most immediate threat not as a conventional military attack, but as a campaign of covert and deniable actions aimed at unsettling Ukraine's allies and eroding Western unity as the war drags on.

Kallas said Russia appeared willing to take greater risks and argued the answer was to increase pressure on Moscow through tougher sanctions, including measures targeting its "shadow fleet" and military-industrial complex.
"Russia's economy is one of its weakest parts, and we need to increase the pressure on it so that they would stop this war," she said.
Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski said such activity was no longer merely a threat.
"They're not just threats; they're actual attacks," Sikorski told Reuters, citing arson, explosions, drone incursions and what Warsaw says was a deliberate cruise missile violation of its territory.

A Russian Mi-8 military helicopter flies in Syria's northeastern Hasakeh province on Feb 4, 2021. (Photo: AFP/Delil Souleiman)

The Polish Army Operational Command said on Wednesday (Sep 23) a Russian military Mi-8 helicopter made a brief incursion into its airspace from the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad.
"Our F-16s are scrambled up almost every day now because you just never know when these drones or missiles that approach might not actually be possible," he said.
Romanian Foreign Minister Oana Toiu told Reuters Bucharest had seen more than 100 incursions by drones or drone fragments onto its territory as Russia intensified attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure near the Danube and Black Sea.
"We do not have data to indicate we're targeted directly, but that doesn't change the responsibility of Russia for the risk it creates," she said.
Romania has responded by closing Russia's consulate in Constanta and coordinating diplomatic measures with European allies, she added.
The Kremlin consistently denies conducting sabotage operations in NATO countries or plotting any confrontation.

NO IMMINENT NATO ATTACK Despite the incidents, ministers drew a distinction between Russia's covert campaign and the prospect of a direct attack on NATO territory.
Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna told Reuters alarmist predictions of an imminent Russian assault on the alliance were misplaced.
"We don’t see that Russia is able and even preparing for some kind of active military aggression against NATO or the European countries," he said, arguing Moscow lacked the capabilities for such an operation while its forces remained heavily engaged in Ukraine.
He said Moscow's campaign was designed primarily to create fear and divisions within Western societies.
"This is mainly meant for creating fear, fear of escalation, to divide us, to play with our unity," Tsahkna said. "The main message is: Don't let Putin play with the fear of escalation," he said, referring to Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Lithuanian Foreign Minister Kestutis Budrys said allied intelligence pointed to a risk that Russia could seek to broaden pressure on NATO countries through attacks on critical infrastructure and other forms of hybrid activity.
"There are some considerations on the Russian side to escalate horizontally, so to say, or geographically," Budrys told Reuters.
The ministers said the best way to counter such tactics was through unity, deterrence and continued support for Ukraine, particularly ahead of winter, when Russia is expected to intensify attacks on energy infrastructure.
Budrys warned that "the cold will be weaponized by Russia" and urged European countries to provide more assistance, arguing support remained patchy across the bloc.
Several ministers argued that firm responses had already shown results. Tsahkna pointed to the sharp reduction in serious Russian airspace violations on NATO's eastern flank following a strong allied reaction to previous incidents.
"Putin is carefully watching," he said. "We have lots of leverage, but we just need to have self-confidence and be clear about our language."

items.title: Ibovespa fecha em queda com exterior desfavorável, sem tirar eleição do radar
items.author: Paula Arend Laier
items.creator: Paula Arend Laier
items.summary: Após duas altas seguidas, o Ibovespa fechou em queda nesta quarta-feira, contaminado pelo cenário externo desfavorável a ativos de risco, em meio ao avanço dos rendimentos dos títulos do Tesouro dos Estados Unidos.
items.body:
Após duas altas seguidas, o Ibovespa fechou em queda nesta quarta-feira, contaminado pelo cenário externo desfavorável a ativos de risco, em meio ao avanço dos rendimentos dos títulos do Tesouro dos Estados Unidos.
Índice de referência do mercado acionário brasileiro, o Ibovespa (.BVSP) recuou 0,86%, a 185.814,09 pontos, após marcar 185.676,38 na mínima e 188.772,33 na máxima do dia.
O volume financeiro somou R$29,68 bilhões, com investidores também analisando nova pesquisa eleitoral no Brasil.
O rendimento do [USN:L6N45F0UJ TEXT:"Treasury"] de 10 anos marcava 5,1038% no final da sessão, com a retomada da alta do petróleo e dados robustos sobre a maior economia do mundo apoiando apostas de alta dos juros norte-americanos em outubro.
Investidores também analisaram os comentários do diretor do Federal Reserve, Michael Barr, de que o banco central dos EUA deu um passo importante na semana passada para "recalibrar" os juros de curto prazo a fim de reduzir a inflação, e que provavelmente precisará implementar [USN:L6N45F0SD TEXT:"novos aumentos"] nas taxas. Em uma decisão unânime na semana passada, os membros do Fed elevaram a taxa de juros de referência para a faixa de 3,75% a 4,00%.
De acordo com o advisor senior da Blue3 Investimentos, Gabriel Macarini, o movimento dos títulos do Tesouro dos EUA foi o principal gatilho para a performance negativa na bolsa, dada a leitura que o Fed seguirá duro por mais tempo.
Em Wall Street, o índice acionário S&P 500 (.SPX) encerrou em baixa de 0,75%.
O barril do petróleo sob o contrato [USN:L1N45F01U TEXT:"Brent"] superou US$103 sem sinais de fato de um avanço diplomático para o Irã, com o presidente iraniano, Masoud Pezeshkian, afirmando que o país nunca irá se render.
A sessão também foi marcada por expectativa para o [USN:L6N45F0JU TEXT:"encontro"] entre o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, e o presidente da China, Xi Jinping, na quinta-feira em Washington.
No Brasil, pesquisa [USN:S0N44P04X TEXT:"Atlas/Bloomberg"] mostrou que o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) voltou a liderar as intenções de voto contra o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) em um eventual segundo turno da eleição presidencial, embora siga o empate técnico.
De acordo com Mateus Hammes, head de investimento da Ludo Capital, as pesquisas continuam mostrando um cenário binário com desfecho em aberto. E o mercado "está cobrando um prêmio de risco por não saber quem governará o Brasil em 2027".
Em paralelo, dados da B3 mostraram nova entrada líquida de estrangeiros das ações brasileiras no último dia 21, ampliando o saldo positivo acumulado em setembro para R$9,635 bilhões, de R$9,230 bilhões até o dia 18.
DESTAQUES

items.title: McDonald’s to create tiered loyalty program to lure repeat visitors
items.author: Waylon Cunningham
items.creator: Waylon Cunningham
items.summary: McDonald’s will shift its loyalty program to a new tiered system, chief marketing officer Morgan Flatley said at the chain’s investor day on Wednesday, in a bid to more sharply differentiate between more frequent and casual customers.
items.body:
McDonald’s (MCD.N) will shift its loyalty program to a new tiered system, chief marketing officer Morgan Flatley said at the chain’s investor day on Wednesday, in a bid to more sharply differentiate between more frequent and casual customers.
The move follows a trend in the restaurant space to adopt tiers and to move away from broad discounting that can hurt profit margins. Starbucks [USN:L6N3YU0WX TEXT:"announced a similar change"] to its loyalty program in January.
McDonald's will seek to attract new loyalty program members and to increase the frequency of purchases by existing members with "highly personalized experiences based on the foods, rituals, and moments that matter most to them,” Flatley said.
Flatley did not say when the tiered revamp would launch, or how many tiers would be in the program, but described three categories of loyalty program members based on how frequently they ate at the chain.
The two most active categories, which total 220 million members worldwide, comprise customers who visit more than once a month as well as those who do so once every 90 days.
The first could be targeted with faster points earnings, early access to limited-time menu items, and invitations to company launch events, she said, while the second could be targeted with online game-like challenges encouraging more visits.
A third group is loyalty members who have not eaten at McDonald’s in a few months, which comprises another 150 million members. “Our goal is to give them a reason to reconsider McDonald's,” she said, saying the company would target them with benefits like a “birthday bonus.”
She said loyalty program members in the United States this year could expect Uber ride credits and subscriptions to the Disney+ streaming service.
CEO Chris Kempczinski said loyalty program members drive about 30% of sales, and that loyalty members tend to eat 2-1/2 times more frequently at the restaurants.
Kate Hogenson, principal consultant at the Mallett Group, a brand-loyalty consulting firm, said McDonald's is smart to try to "move the middle," or to entice occasional diners to eat more frequently.
But "tiers are tough," she said, and the success of it will depend on McDonald's execution. She said at least one sandwich chain that had introduced a tiered program had to pull it back because of a lack of cooperation from franchisees.

items.summary: Executivos de três das principais empresas de inteligência artificial do mundo apresentaram um relatório ao Conselho de Segurança da ONU nesta quarta-feira, em meio a alertas de que sistemas de IA cada vez mais poderosos poderiam, em breve, se aperfeiçoar sozinhos, escapar do controle humano e representar uma ameaça à segurança internacional.
items.body:
Executivos de três das principais empresas de inteligência artificial do mundo apresentaram um relatório ao Conselho de Segurança da ONU nesta quarta-feira, em meio a alertas de que sistemas de IA cada vez mais poderosos poderiam, em breve, se aperfeiçoar sozinhos, escapar do controle humano e representar uma ameaça à segurança internacional.
Entre os que se dirigiram ao conselho de 15 membros durante a reunião anual da Assembleia Geral estavam o presidente-executivo da OpenAI, Sam Altman, o presidente-executivo da Anthropic, Dario Amodei, e o cofundador da Hugging Face, Clément Delangue, três dos executivos mais proeminentes do setor.
“Se mal administrada, acredito até que a IA possa ser um risco para a humanidade como um todo”, afirmou Amodei, da Anthropic, ao Conselho de Segurança.
Governos têm se debatido com a questão de como supervisionar sistemas de IA que avançam mais rápido do que os órgãos reguladores conseguem acompanhar, enquanto os Estados Unidos e a China -- os dois principais atores no desenvolvimento da IA -- permanecem divididos sobre eventuais limites globais à tecnologia ou se ela deve ser deixada, em grande parte, às forças de mercado.
“Para que a IA seja democrática, as decisões mais importantes não podem ser tomadas apenas por laboratórios em San Francisco. Elas devem ser moldadas por meio de processos democráticos e por governos que prestem contas ao povo que servem”, disse Altman ao conselho. “No âmbito internacional, isso exigirá cooperação.”
“Ao longo da nossa história, houve momentos em que países que competem entre si e nem sempre se dão muito bem ainda assim se uniram por interesses comuns e pelo bem coletivo diante de uma nova tecnologia poderosa. Acreditamos que este deve ser um desses momentos”, disse ele.
Yoshua Bengio, canadense considerado um dos “padrinhos da IA” e copresidente do Painel Científico Internacional Independente, criado pela Assembleia Geral da ONU no ano passado, disse ao Conselho de Segurança: “Os perigos são reais e iminentes.”
“Este conselho enfrenta uma ameaça sem precedentes, que nenhum de seus membros escolheria, que ninguém pode conter sozinho e que não respeita as fronteiras que defendemos”, afirmou.
Às vésperas de uma reunião entre o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, e o líder chinês Xi Jinping, em Washington, na quinta-feira, os EUA e a China discutiram a criação de um sistema de notificação para objetivos e ameaças comuns, que abrangeria incidentes relacionados à IA que atinjam o nível de segurança nacional.
Trump disse aos líderes mundiais na Assembleia Geral da ONU na terça-feira que “rejeita qualquer tentativa de construir um esquema globalista para controlar” a IA, descrevendo a tecnologia como incrível, mas observou que os EUA devem agir com cautela.
“Estamos muito à frente da China e de todos os outros, e vamos manter essa vantagem”, disse Trump. “Não vou sufocar o crescimento de algo que será maior do que a Revolução Industrial.”
“Vamos incentivá-la, não contê-la. Vamos acompanhá-la de perto por meio do Departamento de Justiça”, disse.
O secretário-geral da ONU, António Guterres, que vem defendendo uma governança global para a IA, alertou que o rápido avanço da inteligência artificial apresenta riscos que não podem ser ignorados, o que o coloca em desacordo com Trump.
O Conselho de Segurança se reuniu pela primeira vez para discutir os riscos da IA em 2023, quando a China afirmou que a tecnologia não deveria se tornar um “cavalo fora de controle” e os Estados Unidos alertaram contra seu uso para censurar ou reprimir pessoas. O então secretário de Estado dos EUA, Antony Blinken, presidiu uma reunião do Conselho de Segurança sobre IA em 2024.

items.title: Imagem de Flávio Bolsonaro com arma e elefante morto é IA
items.author: Reuters Fact Check
items.creator: Reuters Fact Check
items.summary: Uma imagem do candidato a presidente Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) segurando uma espingarda ao lado de um elefante morto foi produzida com IA, segundo uma ferramenta de detecção do Google.
items.body:
Uma imagem do candidato a presidente Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) segurando uma espingarda ao lado de um elefante morto foi produzida com IA, segundo uma ferramenta de detecção do Google.
Estes são os principais detalhes:
Na imagem sintética, que circula no Facebook , Flávio aparece à frente do elefante, e outros três homens estão atrás do animal abatido. Todos vestem camisetas bege e estampadas.
Uma análise da ferramenta SynthID, do Google, detectou marcas d’água ocultas que indicam que a imagem foi produzida por uma IA da empresa.
Em alguns posts, a foto sintética aparece em uma reportagem da revista piauí, intitulada “O Safári dos Investigados”, que fala sobre uma viagem de Flávio Bolsonaro à África do Sul com investigados pelo esquema de descontos ilegais no INSS.
No entanto, a reportagem original exibe uma imagem em que não há nenhum elefante abatido.
Nela, Flávio está com o senador Weverton Rocha (PDT-MA), o advogado Willer Tomaz, o empresário Carlos Alberto de Sá e três crianças, e não aparece segurando nenhuma arma de fogo.
As camisetas usadas por Flávio e os demais homens na foto da reportagem são similares às retratadas na imagem produzida por IA.
A revista piauí não respondeu de imediato a um pedido de comentário da Reuters.
Veredicto: Mídia sintética. A imagem de Flávio com um elefante morto foi gerada por IA, segundo uma ferramenta de detecção do Google.
Este artigo foi produzido pela equipe da Reuters Fact Check. Envie sugestões de checagem via WhatsApp pelo número (11) 91599-9278. . Leia mais sobre nosso trabalho de checagens de afirmações nas redes sociais aqui .

items.title: Sindicatos de trabajadores de mina chilena de cobre Centinela llaman a rechazar oferta de contrato
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Dos sindicatos de trabajadores de la mina chilena de cobre Centinela, de Antofagasta Minerals, llamaron el miércoles a sus socios a votar en rechazo a una oferta de contrato colectivo presentada por la empresa, lo que abre la posibilidad a una paralización en el yacimiento.
items.body:
Dos sindicatos de trabajadores de la mina chilena de cobre Centinela, de Antofagasta Minerals, llamaron el miércoles a sus socios a votar en rechazo a una oferta de contrato colectivo presentada por la empresa, lo que abre la posibilidad a una paralización en el yacimiento.
Los sindicatos de Minera Esperanza y de Distrito Centinela, que unieron su negociación colectiva, recibieron la última propuesta del proceso formal de diálogo, que tendrá que ser votada hasta el 28 de septiembre.
"La última oferta entregada hoy ni siquiera resuelve la actual discriminación, manteniéndose diferencias que llevan años. Pero de manera relevante tampoco plantea alternativas que aseguren evitar nuevas discriminaciones, como ha ocurrido de manera sistemática los últimos años", dijo un líder sindical a los socios en una comunicación.
Agregaron que "convocarán a sus socios a votar la huelga".
De acuerdo a la legislación chilena, de rechazarse la oferta, las partes todavía deben sentarse a una intermediación gubernamental obligatoria de cinco días, que puede extenderse por igual período de mutuo acuerdo, antes de quedar autorizados para iniciar una huelga.
Hasta el martes, los gremios aseguraron que la negociación estaba en un "punto muerto" ya que la empresa no se habría abierto a discutir la igualdad en los beneficios de los trabajadores, independiente del sindicato al que pertenezcan.
Antofagasta Minerals declina comentar sobre sus negociaciones colectivas.
En tanto, los gremios aseguran estar preparados económicamente para afrontar una eventual huelga "de muchos días" en el yacimiento.

items.title: Taylor Swift announces new music on 'The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore'
items.author: Chandni Shah
items.creator: Chandni Shah
items.summary: Taylor Swift announced an expanded version of her 12th studio album titled "The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore" on Wednesday, with four new songs written after the historic success of the record's release a year ago.
items.body:
Taylor Swift announced an expanded version of her 12th studio album titled "The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore" on Wednesday, with four new songs written after the historic success of the record's release a year ago.
"The Encore" will be released on Friday, Swift said in an Instagram post. "The Life of a Showgirl" was [USN:L2N3VK06G TEXT:"released"] last October and topped several records, with every one of its 12 songs landing in the top 12 of the Billboard Hot 100.
The new tracks were written after "Showgirl" had the biggest debut for an album in modern music history based on album sales and streams, Swift said.
At that time, "I took a trip to Sweden to celebrate with Max (Martin) and Shellback, my two collaborators on this album," the pop superstar said in an Instagram post. "Really we just wanted to reflect and take in how grateful we were for the moment we were in, but there was a studio there and we did what we do when we feel anything at all: We wrote more songs."
The expanded "Showgirl" will feature the single "Patient Zero," which the pop superstar teased and subsequently announced on Tuesday, alongside “Cleveland!,” “Pink Clouding” and “Babylon.”
Martin and Shellback are songwriters who have worked with Swift on several of her studio albums.
Swift's announcement followed her appearance this month in a comedy sketch at television's Emmy Awards that convinced her fans she was teasing new music.
"The Fate of Ophelia," the lead single off "Showgirl," brought in 92.5 million official streams in the US in its opening week, according to Luminate, a firm that tracks music sales.

items.title: ロシア大統領特使が23日訪米、ウィットコフ氏らと会談＝関係筋
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [２３日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[２３日 ロイター] - ロシアのドミトリエフ大統領特別代表が２３日に米国に向け出発し、ニューヨークでウィットコフ和平交渉担当特使とトランプ米大統領の娘婿ジャレッド・クシュナー氏を含むトランプ政権関係者と会談する。複数の関係筋がロイターに対し明らかにした。

関係筋によると、ドミトリエフ氏の訪米はロシアのプーチン大統領の了承を得ており、トランプ政権関係者との会談は国連総会が開かれているニューヨークで行われる。今月初めにロシアの首都モスクワで行われたプーチン大統領と米国代表団との会談を踏まえた協議になるという。

関係筋の１人は、ドミトリエフ氏の訪米の目的は米ロ対話と和平に向けた取り組みを継続することだと述べた。

items.title: Rain, wind could blow Red Sox, Cubs to early end of regular season
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: A major storm heading toward New England this weekend is expected to force the Chicago Cubs and Boston Red Sox into an early end to the regular season.
items.body:
A major storm heading toward New England this weekend is expected to force the Chicago Cubs and Boston Red Sox into an early end to the regular season.
The upcoming three-game series, which starts Friday at Boston, is expected to have playoff seeding implications.
The Boston Globe reported Wednesday that MLB does not plan to move the series to an alternate location despite a storm that will include heavy rain and wind in a regional event commonly known as a nor'easter.
With the worst of the weather expected to begin Saturday night, multiple outlets have reported that a Friday doubleheader is being planned, with a single game on Saturday that would end the regular season for both clubs.
The Red Sox (84-73) were locked into either the second or third wild-card spot in the American League. They entered Wednesday's play as the second wild card with a three-game lead on the Chicago White Sox in the third spot.
The Cubs, Philadelphia Phillies and San Diego Padres all were tied for the top spot the National League wild-card standings at 87-70, with the Arizona Diamondbacks still holding a outside chance at a postseason spot, four games back.
The tight Friday-Saturday schedule would have its advantages for both teams. Both would get an extra day of rest for their pitching staffs heading into wild-card round opening games Tuesday as the remainder of the wild-card field finishes their regular-season schedule Sunday.
--Field Level Media

items.title: 米エネルギー長官、ディーゼル輸出禁止に異論　ホワイトハウスは報道否定
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Nicole Jao

［ニューヨーク／ワシントン　２３日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
Nicole Jao

［ニューヨーク／ワシントン　２３日　ロイター］ -  ライト米エネルギー長官は２３日、ディーゼル燃料の輸出禁止措置は機能せず、ガソリンやジェット燃料の価格を押し上げる恐れがあると述べ、同措置を支持するトランプ大統領と異なる立場を示した。

ライト長官は英エコノミスト誌が主催するイベントで、「ディーゼル輸出禁止という乱暴な手段は絶対に機能しない」と述べた。

ライト長官は「精製所から出るディーゼルを輸出できなければ、保管場所が足りなくなり、米国の精製処理量を減らさざるを得なくなる。それはガソリンとジェット燃料の価格に上昇圧力をかけることになる」と語った。

ライト長官はまた、政権は精製業界と協力し、「精製処理量を減らすような乱暴な手段を用いず、より簡素で自主的、協調的な形で」米国内のディーゼル供給を増やす取り組みを進めていると述べた。ただ具体的な計画には触れず、まだ何も決定していないとした。

ディーゼル価格はこのところ過去最高値を更新しており、１１月の中間選挙を前に農家など利用者の不満が高まっている。自動車利用者団体ＡＡＡによると、２３日時点の米国のディーゼル平均価格は１ガロン＝６．５２ドルと、１年前から７６％上昇している。

トランプ米大統領は２２日、ディーゼル燃料の輸出禁止を支持すると表明した。

ホワイトハウスの当局者は２３日、米国がディーゼル燃料の輸出を９０日間禁止する準備を進めているとする報道を否定した。

米政治専門サイトのポリティコは、米国が９０日間の輸出禁止措置を準備していると報じていた。ライト長官もこの報道を否定した。

items.title: Trump ramps up noncitizen voting prosecutions ahead of midterms
items.author: Andrew Goudsward, Tom Hals
items.creator: Andrew Goudsward, Tom Hals
items.summary: President Donald Trump’s administration is ramping up criminal prosecutions of noncitizens accused of voting in US elections as he presses claims of widespread election fraud ahead of the November midterms.
items.body:
President Donald Trump’s administration is ramping up criminal prosecutions of noncitizens accused of voting in US elections as he presses claims of widespread election fraud ahead of the November midterms.
The US Justice Department has brought criminal charges against about 20 people this month under a law criminalizing “voting by aliens”, roughly 13% of all prosecutions brought under the statute since it was enacted three decades ago, according to a Reuters review of court records and government statements.
The investigative arm of the Department of Homeland Security has mobilized hundreds of agents in all 50 states to aid what a Justice Department official described as a “tier-one priority for the attorney general and for the White House.”
The official, speaking on the condition of anonymity to discuss details of the investigations, said the pace of prosecutions would likely increase in the weeks leading up to the November 3 midterms, which will determine control of the US Senate and House of Representatives.
The spate of recent cases is part of a long-running attempt by the Trump administration to demonstrate that voting by non-US citizens poses a major threat to the security of elections, despite studies showing the practice is rare.
Trump and his supporters say it is part of an organized conspiracy led by Democrats who hope to retake Congress. Trump is pushing Republicans in Congress to toughen up [USN:L6N40414R TEXT:"voting requirements"].
Critics of the administration allege the claims are aimed at diminishing confidence in the vote and potentially laying the groundwork to challenge election results, with polls showing Trump’s Republican Party could face significant losses in November.
The rhetoric about noncitizen voting is "little by little eroding the trust of the public,” Nevada Secretary of State Francisco Aguilar, a Democrat, told Reuters.
Trump administration officials have pointed to the recent cases to push back against Democratic criticism.
“The folks on the other side, the opponents of the president, insist this never happens,” acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter told reporters on Tuesday. “When you have dozens of cases that we brought just in the last few weeks, I think that discourages and defeats their characterization.”
A Reuters review published in July found that prior to Trump’s second term, federal prosecutions for alleged noncitizen voting were extremely uncommon. Many defendants were lawful permanent residents, a trend that has continued in the recent cases.
A [USN:L6N43Z058 TEXT:"separate Reuters review"] published on Wednesday found states may have added more than 30,000 self-declared noncitizens to the nation’s voter rolls since 2000 because of software glitches and clerical errors made while processing their driver's license and state ID applications.
Cases brought by the DOJ in recent weeks allege that defendants registered to vote or cast ballots in recent elections despite knowing they were not US citizens. The recent uptick in prosecutions represents a small fraction of the tens of millions of ballots cast in federal elections.
An official with Homeland Security Investigations, the DHS unit that conducts criminal investigations, said HSI has 1,600 open investigations related to the issue.
A COORDINATED EFFORT The Justice Department has brought charges against 32 people in the last four weeks for noncitizen voting and related offenses, according to a DOJ spokesperson.
Seven of those cases were brought by the US Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Texas, where federal prosecutors received help from the office of Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, the Republican nominee for the US Senate and a [USN:L6N41V0YO TEXT:"Trump ally"].
In one example of the pressure to bring cases, a top DOJ official told senior prosecutors at US attorney’s offices across the country this month that prosecutors could no longer decide on their own to refuse election fraud cases, according to a source briefed on the conversation.
The deputy attorney general's office, staffed by political appointees, would have the final say if agents with the FBI or DHS felt the evidence warranted charges, the source said.
The directive unnerved some on the call given it has traditionally been career prosecutors who decide whether charges are justified in such cases, according to the source. MS NOW first reported details of the meeting.
A DOJ official said the deputy attorney general's office would not intervene in every case where prosecutors think charges are not warranted, but said department leadership would mediate disputes between prosecutors and agents.

items.title: CDC Recognizes Measles Death After Pennsylvania Conflict
items.author: list.metadata.agency
items.summary: The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention confirmed one measles-related death in the US, almost a month after Pennsylvania first reported deaths to the agency.
items.body: (Bloomberg) -- The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention confirmed one measles-related death in the US, almost a month after Pennsylvania first reported deaths to the agency.In an update of its dashboard for measles cases in 2026 on Wednesday, the CDC added one of the four fatalities Pennsylvania has reported so far this year, backing away from a feud with the state over what constitutes a death from measles. The dispute began after Pennsylvania notified the CDC about its first two measles-related deaths in August, Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. publicly questioned them and suggested Democratic Governor Josh Shapiro had fabricated the deaths for political gain. Shapiro blamed Kennedy for sowing distrust in vaccines.When the CDC had not previously included the measles deaths, it said it was working with the Council of State and Territorial Epidemiologists to develop a standard definition for a measles death. Emily Hilliard, spokesperson for the Department of Health and Human Services, said the CDC is still working on developing a standardized definition. The National Center for Health Statistics notified the Atlanta-based CDC that it received a report of a measles-related death, Hilliard said in a statement. “Through its standard process, NCHS verified that the death occurred and that measles was listed as the underlying cause of death.” On Sept. 16, Pennsylvania formally asked for CDC’s Epi-Aid, which provides rapid federal assistance during disease outbreaks, but said it would rescind the request if the agency could not “transparently and accurately communicate” information about the deaths.In response, a spokesperson for HHS said that the agency would not “submit to political blackmail” over critical public health aid.A spokesperson for the Pennsylvania health department said in a statement Sept. 22 that discussions between CDC and the state for federal help are ongoing.The US has reported 3,471 measles cases so far this year through Sept. 17, the nation’s worst outbreak since the early 1990s. Pennsylvania hadn’t recorded a measles-related death in 35 years before this summer. The state’s outbreak this year has now hit 835 cases, with 164 people hospitalized. Less than 1% of the confirmed cases happened in people who had been fully vaccinated against measles.Pennsylvania’s health department has emphasized that getting fully vaccinated with the two-dose measles, mumps and rubella shot is the best form of protection against the highly contagious virus. Nine out of 10 unvaccinated people who come into contact with the virus that causes measles will be infected. It can lead to dangerous complications like pneumonia, brain swelling and death.Last month, President Donald Trump signed an executive order recommending that the MMR vaccine be split into three shots, which would mean parents would have to make more trips to the doctor to get the same protection against diseases for their young children, which could raise the risk that some would miss immunizations.(Updates with latest measles numbers from Pennsylvania in the 10th paragraph.)More stories like this are available on bloomberg.com©2026 Bloomberg L.P.

items.title: Petrobras podría incluir proyecto de gas Syrius en Colombia en su plan de negocios 2027-2031
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Petrobras podría incluir el proyecto de gas natural Syrius, frente a las costas de Colombia, como parte de la curva de producción que presentará en su plan de negocios para el periodo 2027-2031, previsto para finales de este año, siempre y cuando obtenga la licencia ambiental a tiempo, dijo el miércoles una ejecutiva de la compañía.
items.body:
Petrobras podría incluir el proyecto de gas natural Syrius, frente a las costas de Colombia, como parte de la curva de producción que presentará en su plan de negocios para el periodo 2027-2031, previsto para finales de este año, siempre y cuando obtenga la licencia ambiental a tiempo, dijo el miércoles una ejecutiva de la compañía.
Petrobras, que actúa como operadora con una participación del 44,4% en asociación con la estatal colombiana Ecopetrol, ha avanzado en la obtención de la licencia ambiental para el proyecto, pero aún debe concluir las consultas con las comunidades locales, señaló Sylvia Anjos, directora de Exploración y Producción.
"Creo que sí debería aparecer (en la curva de producción). Si logramos esa licencia, es posible que se incluya", dijo Anjos a periodistas durante el congreso de petróleo y gas ROG.e.
"Todavía me falta (...) un número muy reducido de comunidades para aprobar el proyecto ambiental. Si obtengo la licencia ambiental, entonces podré aprobar el proyecto de producción (...) una vez obtenida la licencia, el siguiente paso es la aprobación por parte de la junta directiva", explicó.
La ejecutiva reiteró que el proyecto contempla la construcción de un ducto que transportará el gas desde el lecho marino directamente hasta la costa, sin necesidad de una plataforma.
"Hemos diseñado un proyecto bastante innovador, ya que se trata de gas metano, un gas excelente que no requiere procesamiento alguno, es maravilloso. Así que saldrá del fondo del mar a través del gasoducto hasta llegar a la terminal en tierra. Por lo tanto, no habrá plataforma", afirmó.
Al ser consultada sobre si Petrobras está considerando invertir en Venezuela, Anjos descartó esa posibilidad.
Sin embargo, indicó que se está analizando "todo lo que está disponible en África".
La semana pasada, Petrobras informó que firmó contratos de reparto de producción para la exploración de ocho bloques marítimos en Costa de Marfil "con elevado potencial", en un paso más de la petrolera para ampliar su actividad en la costa occidental de África, al tiempo que busca nuevas oportunidades para realizar descubrimientos y recomponer sus reservas de petróleo para la próxima década.
Además de Costa de Marfil, Petrobras busca oportunidades en países que incluyen Ghana, Santo Tomé y Príncipe, Namibia y Sudáfrica.

items.title: Unions call strike vote at Antofagasta copper mine in Chile
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Two unions representing workers at Antofagasta Minerals' Centinela copper mine in Chile called on workers to hold a strike vote, saying negotiations with the firm had reached a "dead end".
items.body:
Two unions representing workers at Antofagasta Minerals' (ANTO.L) Centinela copper mine in Chile called on workers to hold a strike vote, saying negotiations with the firm had reached a "dead end".
The unions Trabajadores de Minera Esperanza and Trabajadores Distrito Centinela, which joined the collective bargaining, said they received the latest proposal from the formal dialogue process on Wednesday, with voting scheduled between September 26 and September 28.
"The latest offer received today does not even resolve the discrimination, as long-standing disparities remain," said the unions in a statement.
The unions added they are financially prepared to face a possible strike "lasting many days" at the mine.
Under Chilean law, if the offer is rejected, the parties must still undergo a mandatory five-day government mediation, which can be extended for the same period by mutual agreement, before being authorized to start a strike.
Antofagasta Minerals declined to comment on its collective bargaining negotiations.

items.author: TBS NEWS DIG
items.summary: アメリカとイランが間接協議を行い、イラン外務省は、ホルムズ海峡の開放に向けた条件などについて協議したと明らかにしました。 イラン外務省の報道官によりますと、協議は22日に国連総会が開かれているアメリカ・ニューヨークで、カタールを仲介役とした間接形式で行われました。 イラン側は、ホルムズ海峡の開放などに向けた条件として、▼安全な航行ルートをめぐる合意の受け入れや、▼アメリカによる海上封鎖の停止、▼戦 ...
items.body:
イラン・アメリカが間接協議　ホルムズ海峡開放へ条件協議

TBSテレビ

2026年9月24日(木) 04:15

国際

アメリカとイランが間接協議を行い、イラン外務省は、戦闘の終結やホルムズ海峡の開放に向けた交渉再開の条件などについて協議したと明らかにしました。

イラン外務省の報道官によりますと、協議は22日に国連総会が開かれているアメリカ・ニューヨークで、カタールを仲介役とした間接形式で行われました。

イラン側は、戦闘の終結やホルムズ海峡の開放などに向けた交渉再開の条件として、▼ホルムズ海峡の新航路を受け入れることや、▼アメリカによる海上封鎖の停止、▼イランの凍結資産の解除などを示したということです。

こうしたなかロイター通信は23日、イラン政府高官の話として、イランは現在、アメリカ側の回答を検討していると報じました。

ただ、この高官は「依然として双方の立場には多くの隔たりがある」と話しているということで、依然として協議の行方は不透明です。

一方、アメリカのルビオ国務長官は協議について、「意見交換のためのものだった」と説明しました。

そのうえで、「大きな進展だと誤解させたくはないが、少なくとも対話が行われたことは意義深い」としています。

items.body:
＜ロンドン株式市場＞ 

下落して取引を終えた。ＦＴＳＥ１００種は横ばい圏ながら続落。中型株で構成するＦＴＳＥ２５０種指数は０．６７％安と反落した。原油先物価格の上昇を受けたインフレ懸念が相場の重荷となった。

米イランが間接協議を開き、戦闘終結に向けた進展への期待が高まったものの、双方とも姿勢の転換を示さなかった。原油価格が上昇したほか、英１０年債利回りは一時５．３５３％を付けた。

ＦＴＳＥ３５０種石油・ガス株指数は２．２１％高。石油大手のＢＰは２．７％、シェルは２．０％それぞれ上昇した。航空宇宙・防衛株指数は１．３７％高。エンジンメーカーのロールスロイスは１．４％値上がりした。

一方、製薬・バイオテクノロジー株指数は１．５１％安。製薬大手アストラゼネカは１．９％、ＧＳＫ は１．０％それぞれ下落した。

小売りのＪＤスポーツ・ファッションは５．７％安。足元の減益決算を受け、売られた。

ロンドン株式市場：[.LJP]

＜欧州株式市場＞ 

反落して取引を終えた。米イラン情勢に進展の兆しが見られず、原油高と国債利回りの再上昇が相場の重荷となった。主要な地域指数はいずれも下落した。

トランプ米大統領は国連総会で２２日、イランが戦闘終結に向けた合意に応じなければ「壊滅させる」と警告。一方、イランのペゼシュキアン大統領は２３日、米国の圧力に決して屈しないと表明した。５営業日連続で下落していたブレント原油先物は再び１バレル＝１００ドルを超えた。ユーロ圏の指標金利であるドイツの１０年債利回りは一時３．５５０％を付けた。

大半の業種が下落し、ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種銀行株指数は０．４４％、保険株指数は１．７０％、建設・資材株指数は１．２７％、いずれも下落した。一方、石油・ガス株指数は１．２９％上昇した。

オランダの建設コンサルティング会社アルカディスは２．９％安。カナダのエンジニアリング企業ＷＳＰグローバルによる買収提案の取り下げを受け、売られた。

次期の最高財務責任者（ＣＦＯ）を発表したオランダの決済サービス会社アディエンは４．７％安だった。

欧州株式市場：[.FJ]

＜ユーロ圏債券＞　

域内国債利回りが上昇した。原油価格が再び上昇したことに加え、ユーロ圏と米国の両方で予想を上回る経済活動指標が発表され、利上げ観測が強まった。

Ｓ＆Ｐグローバルが発表したユーロ圏の９月の総合購買担当者景気指数（ＰＭＩ）速報値は下落予想に反して５３．１に急上昇し、２０２３年４月以来の高水準を記録した。

９月の米ＰＭＩ速報値は５８．４と、前月の５６．０から上昇し、２１年７月以来の高水準となった。

ＤＺバンクのアナリスト、ルネ・アルブレヒト氏は、「今朝発表されたドイツ、フランス、ユーロ圏全体のＰＭＩデータは、特にサービス部門において予想外に堅調だった」と指摘。「ＰＭＩデータが（債券売りの）一因となったことはたしかだ」と述べた。

市場が依然として中東情勢を注視する中、原油価格は６日ぶりに上昇。ブレント原油先物は２．４％高の１バレル＝１０１．６４ドルとなった。

欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）理事会メンバーのナーゲル独連銀総裁は２２日、エネルギー価格の高騰でインフレ率が目標を上回って推移していることを受け、ＥＣＢが金融政策を巡る判断を行うに当たり原油価格が一段と重要な指標になっているとの認識を示した。

市場はＥＣＢが年内に計約３５ｂｐの追加利上げを実施するとの見方を織り込んでいる。ＰＭＩデータ発表前よりわずかに高い水準となったものの、１８日の約４０ｂｐからは低下している。

ユーロ圏の指標金利であるドイツの１０年債利回りは８ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）上昇の３．５３２％。

ＥＣＢの政策金利見通しに敏感な独２年債利回りは７．５ｂｐ上昇の３．２８３％。

フランス１０年債利回りは１２ｂｐ上昇の４．６１３％と、０８年以来の高水準となった。

フランスは２７年の選挙年を控え、議会の分裂による財政リスクに直面しており、ここ数週間で市場の警戒感が一段と強まっている。

独仏１０年債利回り格差は１０８ｂｐまで拡大した。

items.title: Petrobras pode incluir projeto de gás na Colômbia em plano de negócios 2027-2031
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: A Petrobras poderá incluir o projeto de gás natural Syrius, no mar da Colômbia, como parte da curva de produção a ser apresentada em seu plano de negócios para o período de 2027 a 2031, previsto para o final deste ano, caso consiga aprovar a tempo a licença ambiental, afirmou uma executiva da companhia nesta quarta-feira.
items.body:
A Petrobras (PETR3.SA) poderá incluir o projeto de gás natural Syrius, no mar da Colômbia, como parte da curva de produção a ser apresentada em seu plano de negócios para o período de 2027 a 2031, previsto para o final deste ano, caso consiga aprovar a tempo a licença ambiental, afirmou uma executiva da companhia nesta quarta-feira.
A Petrobras, que atua como operadora com uma participação de 44,4% em parceria com a estatal colombiana Ecopetrol, avançou na obtenção da licença ambiental para o projeto, mas ainda precisa concluir as consultas com as comunidades locais, disse Sylvia Anjos, diretora de Exploração e Produção.
"Acho que deve aparecer sim (na curva de produção), se a gente conseguir essa licença; mas talvez entre", disse Anjos, a jornalistas, durante o congresso de petróleo e gás ROG.e.
"Ainda me falta... um número bem reduzido de comunidades para aprovar o projeto ambiental. Se eu tiver a licença ambiental, aí eu posso aprovar o projeto de produção... tendo a licença, o próximo passo é aprovar na diretoria."
A executiva reiterou que o projeto prevê a construção de um duto que vai levar o gás do fundo do mar diretamente para a costa, sem a necessidade de uma plataforma.
"A gente fez um projeto bastante inovador por ser um gás metano, um gás lindo, que não precisa processar nada, é maravilhoso. Então ele vai sair do fundo do mar, o gasoduto, até chegar no terminal em terra. Então não vai ter uma plataforma", afirmou.
Questionada se a Petrobras está estudando investir na Venezuela, Anjos descartou.
Entretanto, disse que está estudando "tudo que é disponível na África".
Na semana passada, a Petrobras informou ter assinado contratos de partilha de produção para a exploração de oito blocos marítimos na Costa do Marfim "com elevado potencial", em mais um passo da petroleira que expande sua atuação na costa oeste africana, enquanto busca novas oportunidades para realizar descobertas e recompor suas reservas de petróleo para a próxima década.
Além da Costa do Marfim, a Petrobras vem buscando oportunidades em [USN:L6N44I10F TEXT:"países"] que incluem Gana, São Tomé e Príncipe, Namíbia e África do Sul.

items.title: Arizona Senator Mark Kelly to Introduce New AI Workforce Bill
items.summary: Democrat Senator from Arizona Mark Kelly discussed his plans to unveil a new bill aimed at mitigating AI impact on the workforce and said that it is important to generate revenue from AI companies to 'give people options.' items.title: Noboa pide a la ONU “transformarse” y tres acciones para combatir el crimen transnacional
items.author: Carlos Cuevas
items.summary: En su intervención ante la Asamblea General de la ONU, el mandatario ecuatoriano, Daniel Noboa, planteó la necesidad de que la organización sea más eficiente y responda a problemáticas que no existían ...
items.body: Bloomberg Línea — El presidente de Ecuador, Daniel Noboa, intervino en la Asamblea General de la ONU este miércoles planteando tres acciones concretas para combatir el crimen transnacional organizado y la necesidad de que esta entidad se transforme para abordar problemáticas propias del siglo XXI. “Las armas que llegan a nuestras calles cruzaron varios países”, dijo Noboa en la primera parte de su discurso. “Los criminales ya globalizaron su cooperación, comparten rutas, finanzas y tecnología; esa es la realidad que la ONU debe asumir”. Ver más: Ecuador pide a EE. UU. ayuda diaria para combatir un negocio de cocaína de US$30.000 millones Noboa aseguró que, para combatir las economías ilegales, como la del narcotráfico, es necesaria una mayor cooperación entre países, liderada por la ONU. En ese contexto, solicitó: Noboa también lamentó que países de renta media como Ecuador enfrenten vulnerabilidades que el ingreso per cápita no refleja. De ahí otra petición: “Que la cooperación y financiamiento se definan con criterios de vulnerabilidad más justos”. El mandatario ecuatoriano agregó que cree en el multilateralismo y, por ende, en la ONU. Sin embargo, a su juicio, la organización debe adaptarse a los nuevos tiempos. “Ecuador cree en las Naciones Unidas y precisamente por eso quiere una organización capaz de responder al mundo de hoy, no al de 1945. Apoyar es también la voluntad de transformar, por eso apoyamos la iniciativa ONU 80 y la invitamos a responder una pregunta esencial: ¿Qué Naciones Unidas necesita el mundo de hoy? Una organización más eficiente, con capacidad de prevenir, resolver crisis y ayudar a los Estados frente a amenazas que no existían cuando fue creada”. Ver más: BID aprueba préstamo por US$500 millones a Ecuador para promover “estabilidad macroeconómica”

items.title: Brazil's Petrobras may include Colombia gas project in 2027-2031 plan, exec says
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Brazil's state-run oil firm Petrobras may include the Sirius offshore gas project in Colombia as part of the production curve to be unveiled in its 2027-2031 business plan later this year, a company executive said on Wednesday.
items.body:
Brazil's state-run oil firm Petrobras (PETR3.SA) may include the Sirius offshore gas project in Colombia as part of the production curve to be unveiled in its 2027-2031 business plan later this year, a company executive said on Wednesday.
"I think it should appear (in the business plan) if we get the environmental license," said Sylvia Anjos, director of exploration and production, to journalists at an oil industry event.
She added that Petrobras has made progress toward obtaining the license, but still has to conclude consultations with local communities. The firm serves as the operator in the project with a 44.4% stake along with Colombia's Ecopetrol (ECOPETROL.CN) .
The project foresees the construction of a pipeline that would carry gas from the seabed directly to the coast, without the need for a platform, Anjos said.
Petrobras said [USN:L1N40Z0XJ TEXT:"earlier this year"] that it had completed more than half of the prior consultations needed, a legal requirement designed to protect the rights of ethnic communities that may be affected by such projects.

items.title: US drafted a memo condemning UK over West Bank sanctions. It was never released
items.author: Humeyra Pamuk, Alexander Cornwell
items.creator: Humeyra Pamuk, Alexander Cornwell
items.summary: In early September, US officials in Jerusalem and Washington prepared a draft statement attributed to Secretary of State Marco Rubio condemning plans by the UK, France and Canada to block imports from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.
items.body:
In early September, US officials in Jerusalem and Washington prepared a draft statement attributed to Secretary of State Marco Rubio condemning plans by the UK, France and Canada to block imports from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.
The September 8 dated document, previously unreported and which two sources said was driven by David Milstein, an influential aide to US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee, proposed that Rubio describe the countries' [USN:S8N42N05Y TEXT:"actions"] as a series of hostile measures against Israel that contribute to antisemitism.
"These tactics unacceptably draw from the playbook of the antisemitic boycotts, divestments and sanctions movement," the draft document, reviewed by Reuters, said.
The statement was never released.
According to three people familiar with the matter, the statement was not supported by the White House and the State Department's senior leadership.
The people spoke on condition of anonymity.
Instead, speaking to reporters on September 8 in Florida before traveling to Latin America, Rubio refrained from outright criticism of the decision or any particular country.
"Obviously, we’re not going to do what the UK did. We saw their announcement today, but I don’t have any comment on it right now," Rubio said.
The episode illustrates a widening divide between the White House and Trump's senior diplomats in Israel about how best to respond to the expansion of Israeli settlements under Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing government.
It also highlights a growing ideological split within the American right over support for Israel, with polling showing younger Republicans holding an increasingly unfavorable opinion of Washington's closest Middle East ally.
President Donald Trump earlier this year expressed his opposition to settlement expansion, a growing source of friction with Israel's Arab neighbors, but his administration has put little pressure on Israel to change its policy.
That has at times put him at odds with Huckabee, a Baptist minister who is a staunch supporter of settlements and who refers to the West Bank by its biblical name, Judea and Samaria, a term used by the Israeli government but not formally adopted by the US.
Huckabee's aide Milstein last year advocated that the US impose sanctions on the entire International Criminal Court to convince it to drop war crimes charges against Israeli leaders over the Gaza war - a measure the Trump administration has yet to deploy.
In response to questions from Reuters, a senior US official said the draft statement was not prepared in consultation with the State Department or White House.
The US embassy referred questions, including requests for comment from Huckabee and Milstein, to the State Department.
The White House did not respond to a request for comment.
US PUBLIC SUPPORT FOR ISRAEL QUESTIONED US public backing for Israel has fallen since the Gaza war began in 2023, particularly among Democrats. A June Quinnipiac University poll found 48% of voters and 66% of Democrats believe the United States is too supportive of Israel, up from 16% and 20% when the question was first asked in 2017.
While large majorities of Republicans aged 50 and older view Israel positively, younger conservative Americans have grown more critical, a Pew Research Center poll from late March showed. Some 57% of Republicans aged 18-49 have an unfavorable opinion of Israel, up from 50% a year previously.
In December last year, Trump said that he and Netanyahu, whose government has overseen a rapid expansion of settlements, [USN:S0N3XP00A TEXT:"did not"] fully agree on the West Bank following a meeting with the Israeli leader. That September, Trump said he would not allow Israel to annex the territory.
Israel has occupied the West Bank since the 1967 Arab-Israeli War. The United Nations and most countries consider settlements to be illegal under international law governing military occupation. Israel rejects this, viewing the territory as disputed rather than occupied.
Violence by Jewish settlers against Palestinians in the territory has risen sharply this year, some of them emboldened by support from Netanyahu's right-wing government, which includes ministers who are themselves settlers.
Huckabee has publicly [USN:L8N44H0H7 TEXT:"condemned"] the violence and called for perpetrators to be prosecuted. He has also said violent settlers were a minority and do not represent the wider settler community.
Some 500,000 Israeli settlers and 3 million Palestinians live in the West Bank, territory Palestinians have long sought for a future state, along with Gaza and East Jerusalem.

CAPE TOWN, Sept 23 : World Cup winner Patrick Vieira headlines a lengthy list of new coaches in charge of African national teams as the group qualifiers for next year’s Africa Cup of Nations finals kick off on Thursday.
Vieira takes charge of Senegal, where he was born, as they look to recover from a disappointing World Cup where they were expected to pose Africa’s best challenge at the tournament in Canada, Mexico, and the United States but delivered an underwhelming performance that cost their former coach Pape Bouna Thiaw his job.
A total of 21 new coaches will be in charge this week as 48 countries begin the group phase of the qualifiers. The list includes six of the 10 African countries who competed at the World Cup.
Vieira was only a child when he and his mother left Dakar for France, whom he helped win the 1998 World Cup.

“I have lots of flashes, such as the place where I used to play football with a tennis ball,” he said after returning to the country as an adult.
However, there is no home debut for Vieira this month with Senegal playing Mozambique and Ethiopia away and then playing a friendly against the Comoros in Marseille.
PAST CUP OF NATIONS WINNERS BACK IN COACHING ROLES
Winning Cup of Nations coaches Aliou Cisse (Senegal 2021) and Herve Renard (Zambia 2012 and Ivory Coast 2015) have new jobs, with Cisse coaching Angola, who face Egypt in Cairo on Friday. Renard has an equally tough return to the role of Ivory Coast coach as they host neighbours Ghana.
Renard was drafted in as an emergency to coach Tunisia at the World Cup, after Sabri Lamouchi was dismissed following a heavy defeat in their first game. The North Africans have since appointed Moin Chaabani, a former international defender, to revive their fortunes.
Sebastien Migne is the new coach of Gabon, who begin their campaign away to Morocco on Friday. The Frenchman should know their opponents well, having coached Haiti when they twice led Morocco in a World Cup group game in Atlanta before losing 4-2.
There is also a return for 78-year-old Claude Le Roy, as coach of Congo, who are away against Namibia on Thursday. Le Roy last coached Togo five years ago.
It will be the veteran French coach’s 12th national team appointment and a second stint with the Congolese, where he was coach from 2013 to 2015.
Le Roy holds the record for the most tournament appearances (9) and matches (38) coached at the Cup of Nations finals.

(Editing by Toby Davis)

items.title: ベッセント米財務長官、中国の何立峰副首相と再び会談－首脳会談前に
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： ベッセント米財務長官は23日、中国の何立峰副首相と再び会談した。両氏は米中間の経済協議を主導しており、20日にニューヨークで会談したばかり。今回の協議は、習近平国家主席が米国に到着し、トランプ大統領と会談する数時間前に行われた。

ベッセント氏は会談後、Xへの投稿で、何氏と「実質的な協議」を行ったと説明。「米国の労働者、農家、企業を守る意義ある約束を取り付けるとともに、米国の経済・国家安全保障上の利益を推進することに引き続き重点を置いた」と述べた。

協議はホワイトハウスに近い世界銀行本部で行われたと、事情に詳しい関係者が明らかにした。世銀自体は協議に関与していないという。

ベッセント氏と何氏はそれぞれ1時間余り、世銀内に滞在した。何氏は午前11時40分、李成鋼商務次官（国際貿易交渉代表）とともに本部を出た。その後、廖岷財政次官も退出した。李氏と廖氏はいずれも20日にニューヨークで行われた会談にも出席していた。

ニューヨークでの協議では、米中当局者はAIや貿易、投資を巡る数時間に及ぶ話し合いを前向きに評価した。李氏は「良い雰囲気」で行われたと述べ、ベッセント氏も協議は「非常に成功した」と評価していた。

items.title: World's largest copper mine halts operations after worker death
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Operations at the world's largest copper mine, BHP's Escondida mine in Chile, were suspended on Wednesday after a worker was killed in an accident, the firm said.
items.body:
Operations at the world's largest copper mine, BHP's (BHP.AX) Escondida mine in Chile, were suspended on Wednesday after a worker was killed in an accident, the firm said.
BHP said the worker had been killed while carrying out maintenance work. The union representing the site had previously told Reuters that the accident involved a front-end loader frequently used by the industry.
"All operational activities at the mine have been suspended," BHP said in a statement, without giving a timeline for when they may restart.
Typically in Chile, mines may only kick off activities after a fatal incident once inspectors verify that conditions are safe enough for a restart.
Escondida is located in Chile's Atacama Desert. BHP operates the mine, while Rio Tinto (RIO.L) holds a 30% stake and Japan-based JECO Corp 12.5%.
BHP had estimated the site would produce up to 1.28 million metric tons of the red metal this year.

items.title: US lawmakers propose overhaul of China tech review before Trump-Xi talks
items.author: David Shepardson
items.creator: David Shepardson
items.summary: The Republican chair of the US House Energy and Commerce Committee and the panel's top Democrat unveiled bipartisan legislation to overhaul a federal process that blocks Chinese technology from entering the US market, as President Donald Trump prepares to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday.
items.body:
The Republican chair of the US House Energy and Commerce Committee and the panel's top Democrat unveiled bipartisan legislation to overhaul a federal process that blocks Chinese technology from entering the US market, as President Donald Trump prepares to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday.
The bill would rewrite procedures governing the Federal Communications Commission's "Covered List," which has become a central tool in Washington's efforts to restrict Chinese technology on national security grounds. The move comes amid a broader US-China struggle over trade and technology.
The legislation, first reported by Reuters, signals congressional concern about how the FCC is using its authority to restrict Chinese technology.
Representatives Brett Guthrie and Frank Pallone said in a joint statement the legislation would change how products are added to the FCC's Covered List and require the agency to seek input from other government agencies before determining whether foreign technology poses an unacceptable national security risk.
“The current process for identifying and barring malicious foreign technology has worked in many cases, but lacks the transparency, consistency, and clarity needed to meet our long-term national security needs as technology rapidly advances," the lawmakers said on Wednesday.
The Covered List has been used by the FCC to ban new Chinese drones, robots, routers, power inverters and other equipment from Chinese companies and has been one of the most significant parts of the Trump administration's China policy. Reuters reported last month the FCC could use the list to ban imports of new models of [USN:L1N43P156 TEXT:"Chinese optical transceivers "]that are crucial to data centers.
Trump and Xi are scheduled to hold talks in Washington on Thursday.
FCC Chair Brendan Carr did not immediately comment on the lawmakers' proposal.
SUDDEN DISRUPTIONS The proposal would also give Congress the ability to reverse FCC Covered List determinations and require input from the Commerce Department before determining specific foreign gear poses unacceptable risks to national security.
The FCC would be required to report to Congress at least seven days before placing any technology on its Covered List and make clear the FCC does not have to retroactively review or revoke any equipment authorization issued before a company or product was added to the Covered List.
That aims to offer "stability to American consumers and companies so that they do not face a sudden disruption by the placement of certain technology or equipment on the FCC’s covered list."
In June, the FCC used the designation to ban the import of previously approved equipment from a group of Chinese manufacturers including Huawei, Dahua (002236.SZ) , ZTE (000063.SZ) and Hikvision (002415.SZ) .
The FCC's actions aim to push Chinese gear out of technology supply chains and spur domestic manufacturing. "I don't think it's an exaggeration to say FCC has become the center of gravity for competitive actions towards China in this Trump term," said Eric Sayers of the American Enterprise Institute in Washington.

AMSTERDAM, Sept 23 : Germany coach Juergen Klopp refused to make any promises of silverware on Wednesday but said signs of progress should be visible when his side face the Netherlands in his first match in charge in the Nations League on Thursday.
The former Liverpool manager succeeded Julian Nagelsmann in July after Germany's shock 2026 World Cup exit.
Nagelsmann had said following Germany's Euro 2024 quarter-final defeat that he was sad he would have to wait two years to lift the World Cup, a prediction that came back to haunt him when his side were eliminated by outsiders Paraguay this summer.
Klopp was asked about his remark at the start of his Liverpool tenure that he would probably have won a title if he was still in the job four years later. He went on to win a string of trophies, including the Premier League and Champions League titles.

He was far more circumspect on Wednesday. "I don't want to promise anything," Klopp told a press conference. "What I can say is we will try and that's what it is about now. That's where we are at the moment."
Four-times world champions Germany have been eliminated early at the last three World Cups and have tasted no major international success since lifting their last World Cup in 2014.
Klopp raised eyebrows last week by naming two separate squads for two sets of two matches in the coming days as he rebuilds the national team ahead of Euro 2028.
"I am in charge of the senior team and my task is to take the football there so that we are in with a chance to win every game we play," Klopp said. "It won't work every day but we are working at it. I hope we can see some things already tomorrow." 
"We need to take steps and the boys are ready for that," he said.
After visiting the Netherlands on Thursday, Germany host Greece on Sunday and Serbia on October 1 before travelling to Greece three days later.
